\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability under Lipschitz composition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.integrable_lipschitz_comp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.integrable_lipschitz_comp}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be integrable,
and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be Lipschitz with some constant $c\ge 0$. Then the
function $\omega\mapsto\psi(U(\omega))$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz stability of integrals in $L^2$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_integral_sub_le_two_norm}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_integral_sub_le_two_norm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.integrable_lipschitz_comp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $U,V\in L^2(\mu)$. If $\psi:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then
\[
\left|\int_\Omega\psi(U)\,d\mu-\int_\Omega\psi(V)\,d\mu\right|\le c\,N_2(U-V),
\]
where $N_2$ denotes the real-valued random-variable norm at exponent $2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second norm of multilinear polynomial evaluations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.polynomial_two_norm_eq_l2Norm}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.polynomial_two_norm_eq_l2Norm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.expect_eval_sq, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$
assign a real coefficient to each subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Suppose
$X_0,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ are mutually independent real random variables on this space, each
has finite fourth moment, and each has mean $0$ and second moment $1$. Then the
$L^2(\mu)$ norm of the random variable $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}
F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ equals the uniform $L^2$ norm of the Boolean-cube function
$x\mapsto\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}F(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in
S}\sigma(x_i)$ and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz stability for multilinear random polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_polynomial_integral_sub_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_polynomial_integral_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_integral_sub_le_two_norm, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.polynomial_two_norm_eq_l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $F,G$ be real
coefficient families indexed by subsets of $[n]$, and let
$X_1,\ldots,X_n:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be independent random variables. Suppose each
$X_i\in L^4(\mu)$, $\int X_i\,d\mu=0$, and $\int X_i^2\,d\mu=1$. For every $c\ge0$ and
every $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\int\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in
S}X_i\right)d\mu-\int\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}G(S)\prod_{i\in
S}X_i\right)d\mu\right|\le c\,\|P_{F-G}\|_2,
\]
where $P_{F-G}(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(F(S)-G(S))\chi_S(x)$ and the norm is taken under
the uniform measure on the Boolean cube.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$
is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then
\[
\left|\E[\psi\circ f]-\E[\psi\circ g]\right|\le c\,\|f-g\|_2,
\]
where expectation and the $L^2$ norm are taken with respect to the uniform measure on
the Boolean cube.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_gaussian_extension_sub_le_l2Norm}

Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$
is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then the difference between the expectations of

\[
\left|\int_{\mathbb R^n}\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in
S}z_i\right)d\gamma^{\otimes n}(z)-\int_{\mathbb
R^n}\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat g(S)\prod_{i\in S}z_i\right)d\gamma^{\otimes
n}(z)\right|\le c\,\|f-g\|_2,
\]
where $\widehat f(S)=\E[f\chi_S]$ and $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, and the norm
